fixes.explanation: Miriam it is. The text says it plainly: "There Miriam died and was buried." She's Moses and Aaron's sister (Numbers 26:59), and the text gives her passing just one short sentence. I think that's a heavy way to start the day.

Water, friend. "Now there was no water for the congregation…" Everything else in this scene grows out of that one problem. People can put up with a lot, but a whole crowd with empty cups gets loud FAST. Verse 2 says they gathered against Moses and Aaron.

Not this time, friend. The text says they gathered against Moses and Aaron, not alongside them. Then verse 3 says the people quarreled with Moses. What the text shows in these verses is a quarrel, not a prayer.

Midian's a real place, but it's not the one in this complaint. The people say, "Why have you led us up out of Egypt to bring us to this wretched place?" Egypt is the place they name. They're complaining about where they are now, and Midian never comes up.

Strikes. "…Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff…" Look back at verse 8 and see what the LORD told them to do to the rock. The text says what Moses did, and it says twice. Hold onto that, because the scene isn't done yet.

True. "…a great amount of water gushed out, and the congregation and their livestock were able to drink." A great amount, friend. The thirsty crowd and their animals could finally drink, and I bet that was a LOUD sigh of relief. The scene doesn't end here, though.

Not false, friend. The text says "…a great amount of water gushed out, and the congregation and their livestock were able to drink." The water came, and the people and the animals were able to drink it. What happens next is the part that stings.

Battles aren't part of this verse. The LORD says, "Because you did not trust Me to show My holiness in the sight of the Israelites…" That's what they didn't trust Him to do. This scene at the rock is about water, a staff and a thirsty crowd.

False is right. The LORD says to Moses and Aaron, "…you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them." The land is still given to the people, but these two won't be the ones bringing them in. Verse 13 then calls these the waters of Meribah.
